findings.title: Promise recognized through its realized result
findings.claim: The hearers' praise accompanies recognition that their Lord's promise has passed into an enacted result: the focus joins وَعْدُ رَبِّنَا to مَفْعُولًا, echoing the completed-promise formula at 17:5 and 73:18; 7:44 voices another group's recognition of its Lord's promise, while 26:226 supplies the contrasting pattern of speech without action.
findings.mechanism: The promise at 17:108:6 is the carrier; مَفْعُولًا at 17:108:8 and the repeated promise/result wording in 17:5 and 73:18 are independent triggers. The recognition in 7:44 and the speech-without-deed contrast in 26:226 meet the focus's وَعْدُ / مَفْعُولًا relation. That contact makes the uttered praise read as recognition of a word that has reached action.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear praise as temporal recognition of a promise becoming an event, with historical and eschatological instances remaining distinct.
findings.containment: The focus still says that the Lord's promise is made real. The contexts are analogues, not one identified promise: 17:5 concerns a historical event, 73:18 an eschatological scene, and 7:44 different speakers. The focus does not specify which promise is meant.

epistemic.reason: The focus words and trusted cross-run support ground the promise/result relation, and exact target Arabic supplies the wider parallels. Target morphology is not supplied for those contexts, so the cross-context relation remains qualified and does not identify the promise's referent.

findings.claim: Beside the surah's description of Satanic promises as delusion, the focus's وَعْدُ رَبِّنَا لَمَفْعُولًا lets سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّنَا carry an additional contrast: the Lord's promise is stated as realized, while deceptive assurance is the counterpattern.
findings.mechanism: The focus praise is the carrier; 17:64 explicitly calls Satan's promises delusion and returns through the focus's promise/result relation. Their contact makes the praise articulate freedom from the mismatch between a promised word and a deceptive assurance.
findings.reader_payoff: The praise gains a specific relation to reliability: it accompanies a promise named as realized against a wider example of false assurance.
findings.containment: 17:64 concerns Satan's promises and does not identify the focus speakers with that scene or specify the focus promise's content. The ordinary declaration of transcendence remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The legacy support nominates the relation, while the focus surface, accepted branch facet, and exact 17:64 target Arabic independently ground a bounded contrast. The interpretation remains contextual.

findings.mechanism: The focus verb يَقُولُونَ and noun وَعْدُ are the carriers. In 10:48 and 21:38, speakers use the same say/promise frame to demand a time; the focus pairs it with a completed-result predicate. That contact changes the line into a recognition response alongside, rather than an erasure of, the timing challenge.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the focus's statement against a recurring question about when the promise arrives, without assuming the voices belong to the same scene.
findings.containment: The external questioners are not identified with the focus speakers, and the focus is not asserted to reply to a particular one of those verses. Both the question and recognition remain visible.

findings.title: Praise within an embodied response to recitation
findings.claim: The focus's spoken سُبْحَٰنَ can be heard within a wider response pattern in which recited signs or reminders bring prostration, glorification, and humility; one supplied parallel also joins recitation to weeping.
findings.mechanism: The focus praise is the carrier, with يَقُولُونَ identifying it as voiced. In 32:15, reminders lead to prostration, tasbih with praise, and freedom from arrogance; in 19:58, recited verses are followed by prostration and weeping. These contexts return through the focus's glorification and speech, widening the utterance into an element of embodied reception.
findings.reader_payoff: The declaration is perceptible as both praise and part of a recurring bodily response to recitation.
findings.containment: The focus itself states the praise, not the full posture-and-tears sequence. The wider verses are parallels with distinct audiences, not a claim that every response is identical.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and exact target Arabic support the response pattern, while the cross-ayah integration is contextual and target morphology is not supplied.

The fulfilled promise is thereby heard in relation to the sovereignty of the Lord named by the speakers.
findings.mechanism: رَبِّنَا and سُبْحَٰنَ are the focus carriers. The independent 39:67 image of dominion and its own tasbih supplies the trigger; the contact joins the focus's Lord-title and praise to sovereign authority over creation.

findings.containment: The focus does not itself describe the earth or heavens or explicitly enumerate divine sovereignty. Those details enter only through 39:67, and they do not identify the focus promise.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and target Arabic provide a clear contextual contact, but the transfer of the sovereignty image to the focus is interpretive and the target morphology is not supplied.

findings.mechanism: The focus وَعْدُ is the carrier. In 48:20, a divine promise is followed by an expedited share; that separate realization pattern contacts the focus promise and adds a temporal scale in which an outcome may arrive by portions.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can retain the focus's accomplished result while perceiving that divine promise and historical realization need not unfold all at once in every wider parallel.
findings.containment: 48:20 concerns a different promise and does not establish that the focus event is partial or still pending.

epistemic.reason: The connection supplies exact Arabic describing another divine promise and an expedited portion; applying its staged pattern to the focus is analogical, not evidence that the referents are identical.
